key_insight: Four vision backbones achieved similar brain tumour segmentation performance after LoRA adaptation but showed different internal changes and effects on Alzheimer's classification.
clinical_relevance: For research on brain MRI, segmentation accuracy alone may not identify models that preserve performance across tasks; this study does not evaluate cancer drug discovery or clinical outcomes.
method: Adapted DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM and BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16 backbones using LoRA.
Examined attention divergence, weight changes and activation patching to identify causally relevant layers.
Tested LoRA restricted to early-to-mid layers against full-layer adaptation.
evidence_signal: Across six datasets covering tumour segmentation and Alzheimer's classification, mean segmentation Dice was 78–81%; adaptation improved classification for DINOv3 but degraded it for the other three backbones.
watch_item: Layer-restricted LoRA reduced classification degradation in the affected backbones, but broader generalisation and clinical utility remain unestablished.
paper_title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
